text:
jordan (infra): seeing sustained east-west packet skew in usw2 gpu-pool rack r4-azb. streaming token responses hit grpc deadlines, clients see token stalls. started ~15:10 PST
maria (runtime): saw p99 token latency jump and a few 504s on /v1/stream. correlating with infra graphs now
jordan (infra): net metrics show out-of-order arrivals + gap bursts, not classic loss. NIC irq/coalescing counters are spiking on affected hosts
sam (sre): region-wide or rack-local? any retires in place?
jordan (infra): localized to r4-azb; 8 hosts. all Mellanox CNX drivers, fw v14.2. not a global cloud issue
ryan (neteng): this smells like NIC interrupt coalescing + microburst scheduling on the switch causing packets to seem reordered at the TCP layer
tess (oncall): can we do a quick mitigation? disabling GRO/GSO/TCP offloads temporarily? :eyes:
jordan (infra): doing a canary: running on host gpu-azb-07 -> `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`
maria (runtime): also lower the runtime RPC aggressiveness: increasing streaming grace to 800ms so we don't hit deadlines mid-spike
devops-bot: Deploy job #4521 started by jordan (infra)
jordan (infra): collecting tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/usw2-coalesce.pcap 'tcp'`
jordan (infra): quick obs: after disabling offloads reorder decreased but not eliminated. suggests switch side queuing + interrupt batching. switch counters show high Tx coalescing and CPU steal moments
ryan (neteng): please paste `ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "tx_queue|rx_queue|coalesced"` and switch port counters (if available)
jordan (infra): counters snippet:
```
rx_packets: 1345678
rx_errors: 3
tx_packets: 1323456
tx_queue_0_intr: 46321
tx_queue_1_intr: 45899
coalesced_rx: 1294
coalesced_tx: 1110
```
maria (runtime): runtime logs line: `streaming: stall detected, token_index=128, last_packet_gap=210ms` - repeats during the noise window
sam (sre): opening incident ENG-2026-014, P2. timeline anchored to 2026-02-14T15:10:00Z
ryan (neteng): plausible fixes: (1) firmware rollback to last-known-good (14.0) for affected NICs, (2) tune IRQ affinity to spread queues, (3) check switch ASIC microburst counters and egress shaping. I can run fw downgrade on 2 hosts as canary
jordan (infra): scheduling canary downgrade on gpu-azb-07/08 at 15:45 PST. will monitor token p99 and packet sequence metrics
maria (runtime): temporary runtime change: increase grpc streaming deadline to 3s + enable retry-on-fallback for streaming endpoints. pushing now to reduce customer visible errors
tess (oncall): post a status page note? visible p99 impact but majority of requests succeed. recommend a short advisory :thumbsup:
jordan (infra): canary results: after fw rollback on 07/08 we saw ~70% reduction in reorder events and token stalls. looks promising
ryan (neteng): good signal. plan: progressive firmware rollback across rack in 2,2,4 batches with 10m ramp. also will audit IRQ affinity and disable aggressive coalescing defaults
sam (sre): timeline & owners: neteng=fw-rollout, infra=canary/monitor, runtime=grace/revert. target to stabilize p99 within 24h
jordan (infra): followups: collect full pcaps from 3 hosts, export switch logs, and check if any other racks show early signs
maria (runtime): once stable for 24h we'll revert the streaming deadline tweak and re-evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs
ryan (neteng): noted. filing neteng ticket NET-439 with fw image and rollback playbook
jordan (infra): action items summarized: 1) fw rollback (canary -> rack), 2) IRQ affinity audit, 3) switch egress shaping review, 4) collect pcaps + correlation dashboard
sam (sre): incident ENG-2026-014: assigned -> neteng, infra, runtime. will close after 24h of stable p99
jordan (infra): last observed small reorder spike at ~15:59 PST, p99 back to baseline by 16:20 PST. monitoring continues
maria (runtime): thanks all. after the rollback we saw tokens resume streaming without stalls in the canary hosts :thumbsup:
tess (oncall): updating customers on status page and will keep watch overnight
jordan (infra): will post final RCA here once we have switch vendor notes and fw root cause. end of thread for now.
